text: The conduct check runs as a conductCheck branch of InstructionWorkflow on task queue rwb-partner in namespace rwb-recovery, unattended under the rwb-partner service identity, and it reads the sample of partner contacts and complaints through the owners' reads and never as a table of rwb-partner. FSD S9 A2.13.2 names the trigger as a completed ACE batch, an event or a timer without a name, a topic or a length, and the Ownership Map gives S9 no job, so the trigger binding carries the placeholder and no Schedule is created.
why: FSD S9 A2.13.3.3 names "None; runs unattended" as the primary actor, the Ownership Map gives S9 exactly one workflow and no job, and the platform rule is Temporal for a step and a Schedule for a timer job. Separately, no source gives the sample an entity, a field list or an owner: the Logical Data Model has no complaint table, TSD S9 T3.1 gives three partner tables with no contact or complaint column, FSD S9 A2.13 has no field catalog, and the legacy data table names only partner, decision_log_entry and rule_row. Declaring a Schedule or an event would contradict the ownership rows, and a local contact or complaint table would duplicate another module's fact and break the schema boundary.

impact: The check is an unattended workflow branch, the sample is a consumed contract with a fake, the service owns no contact or complaint table, and no Schedule, Quartz row or shared job table is created

A builder may not invent a rule ID, so the record cites the published rows the behaviour obeys and the missing domain stays a gap for the rule owner.

text: The re-selection of an affected case is a Temporal command from the conductCheck branch to rwb-case, one command per case, under R-UNI-45; this service writes no case row, moves no case state and holds no timer, and the command's name and answer shape are Not specified in the source documents (CG-B2-S9-014-1; ASM-B2-S9-014-3).
why: R-UNI-45's to_state is ROUTE_D6_REOPEN, a route state of the case, and TSD S9 T4 says the module has no case state machine of its own. The case, its route state and its timer rows are P3's, so the recall cannot be completed inside rwb-partner, and the alternatives — a REST call from a business step or a new event — are rejected by the call-type rule and by the two events the service owns.

text: A finding becomes a breach when the Conduct and QA officer upholds it; only an upheld breach moves the partner and the work. The suspension is written as partner.panel_status SUSPENDED, the only suspension value LOV-PANEL carries, and the recall as partner_instruction.status RECALLED, and this key adds no table, no column and no state value.
why: R-UNI-29's condition is "a conduct or complaint breach is upheld against the partner" and its action column says "Suspend allocation, recall the affected cases, report to the partner review", while FSD S9 A2.13.2 step 3 only says a task is raised where a person is needed. The word "upheld" has no definition, so a builder has to fix where the person's decision sits and mark it as an assumption; a finding column or a breach column would change two published tables and need a DB story.

why: VR-S9-013-1 and FSD S9 A1.4 make today's business date a precondition of every module action and give a message for the stale case, while DP-05 and the context pack give the ACE views to rwb-source-data alone. Reading the view directly would break the grant rule and inventing a local date check would judge a sample the Workbench cannot vouch for.

text: The check is idempotent per partner and check date: one record, one suspension, one recall set and one clock, and a repeat of the same partner and date answers the record already written through the idempotency library of DP-03.
why: The platform error, pagination and idempotency baseline is the platform library's (Architecture v5 slide 11) and TSD S9 T-A.2 gives the service an Idempotency-Key rule for its write operations. A timed or repeated branch with no key would write a second record for the same finding and escalate a service level twice.

text: The conduct check publishes and consumes no event: the service owns exactly EV-20 InstructionIssued and EV-21 PartnerResultSubmitted and a finding is neither, so the breach reaches the partner review forum through the reporting read model built from the decision records rather than through a third event.
why: The Ownership Map gives the service two events, both about an instruction and its result, so publishing either on a finding would report a fact that did not happen. REQ-S9-007 asks for conduct and complaint data to be reported to the partner review forum, and rwb-reporting builds its read model from events and records, which needs no new producer here.
